current.text: Verify that different parsers used in the application for the same data type (e.g., JSON parsers, XML parsers, URL parsers), perform parsing in a consistent way and use the same character encoding mechanism to avoid issues such as JSON Interoperability vulnerabilities or different URI or file parsing behavior being exploited in Remote File Inclusion (RFI) or Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.

master.text: Verify that different parsers used in the application for the same data type (e.g., JSON parsers, XML parsers, URL parsers), perform parsing in a consistent way and use the same character encoding mechanism to avoid issues such as JSON Interoperability vulnerabilities or different URI or file parsing behavior being exploited in Remote File Inclusion (RFI) or Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.

predecessors.text: Verify that all application components use the same encodings and parsers to avoid parsing attacks that exploit different URI or file parsing behavior that could be used in SSRF and RFI attacks.

summaries.body:
The 5.0 mapping records V1.5.3 as MODIFIED and moved from 4.0.3 V13.1.1, which required that all application components use the same encodings and parsers to avoid parsing attacks that exploit different URI or file parsing behavior usable in SSRF and RFI.

On 21 February 2019 Andrew van der Stock opened #513, saying the control seemed unimportant until Orange Tsai’s Black Hat talk on abusing URL parsers, and that the CWE should be 175 not 116. Jim Manico replied that the talk showed why it mattered. Mapping and that predecessor, not the 4.0 V1.5.3 input-validation slot (#943), are the origin.

Andrew van der Stock’s 26 February 2019 commit resolved #513 on V13.1.1 after asking to rephrase why mismatched parsers matter and pointing at Tsai’s URL-parser SSRF paper. The 5.0 text keeps RFI and SSRF but names JSON, XML, and URL parsers, requires the same character encoding mechanism, and adds JSON Interoperability as an example alongside URI or file parsing behavior.

Roel Storms’s 25 March 2021 #943 commits tagged V1.5.3 are the 4.0 architecture input-validation requirement, not this parser-consistency clause. Isaac Lewis’s 28 October 2021 rollback “to 4.0.3 state” on V1.5.3 is the same reused slot. V12.3 RFI/SSRF wording (#798) is a related file-chapter discussion, not this control’s sentence.

decisions.statement: Andrew van der Stock kept a same-parser/same-encoding requirement after citing Orange Tsai’s Black Hat URL-parser SSRF work as the reason the clause matters, and preferred CWE-175 over CWE-116.
